title: records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [WATCHME(every_journaled_write_names_a_known_caller):waiting] -> PROVED
author: CC
from_idea: none, because it was born in conversation on 2026-09-13 and ruled in the same breath (Akien: 'this is the P0 we tackle first ... approved thru PROVED RULED BLESSED FROM ON HIGH'); the ruling packet CairnCommons/decisions/2026-09-13-records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door.json is the captured prose, opened right after this firing
owner: CC builds it; cairn/tools/artifact is a TOOL (users, not owners — Law 6): the journal it appends is the record repo's state, owned by whoever owns that repo's records, and the door gates nothing at its own address
pre_approval: Akien, 2026-09-13, verbatim: 'good assessment. and this is the P0 we tackle first. well done sir. approved thru PROVED RULED BLESSED FROM ON HIGH' — the build and the crossings to PROVED are pre-approved; the ruling packet is opened beside this ticket.
intention: Every record of truth (tickets, troubles, state, history, validations) changes only through one journaled door that measures WHO wrote by the caller's cgroup ancestry rather than by a claim, so an unexplained change is physics-visible and parks as a ruling for Akien instead of standing as truth.
why: Akien, 2026-09-13: 'the problem with stopping there is that then i'm on the hook for those edits. so we have to build a machine that you must use to update .artifacts and the job of the machine will be in part to assure that a hand edits only happen with an explicit from me to allow that.' And: 'the machine does an introspective call stack check and records who called it. the gates can trigger the mechanism (normal flow), command line (me), and you.' The lived symptom that bore it: ticket 481221f45884 stands at [PROVED] with no crossing in the harbor journal — its cursor was moved by hand (commit 42e3db0, 2026-09-10), and nothing in the system could say so until a reader compared two records by eye. 'Records go through their door' is a memory and a paragraph today; 145 code sites in 69 files write these paths with write_text (census 2026-09-13).
how:
One tool, cairn/tools/artifact: write(path, content, verb, why) that (1) reads its own process ancestry through cairn.tools.cgroup to classify the caller as gate (cairn-*.service unit), CC (superclaude scope) or Akien (login shell) — kernel truth, not a field; (2) appends {path, sha_before, sha_after, verb, caller, stack, prev_entry_sha} to a hash-chained journal beside the records; (3) the pre-commit hook refuses to commit any record whose on-disk hash is not the journal's last sha_after — catching hand edits, git surgery and CC alike at the one point everything passes; (4) a 'hand-edit' verb parks a change and opens a ruling packet, Akien signs or the door reverts to the last journaled state. The existing per-class doors (validation store, history append, ticket cast, trouble clear) become callers. Second ticket: rename the five classes to one extension (.artifact) THROUGH the door so the migration is its first proof. Third: a counting learning block over the journal (prediction = frequency, error = exception).

BUILDER'S ANSWERS (from the cast's builder_check, so the build re-derives nothing):
Questions a Haiku-level builder would need answered, and the answer each gets written into the ticket's how: (1) What exactly is the journal entry schema? {path (repo-relative), sha_before (sha256 of bytes or 'absent'), sha_after, verb (one of: cast, append, seal, clear, ruling, hand-edit, rename, bulk), caller {class: gate|cc|akien|unknown, cgroup: raw path, unit: cairn-*.service or null}, stack: [top 6 frames as file:line:function], why: free text from the caller, count: int (1 unless bulk), at: ISO-8601 UTC, prev: sha256 of the previous entry's canonical JSON or 'genesis', entry: sha256 of this entry's canonical JSON with entry=''}. (2) Where does the journal live and how is it found from a record path? Walk up from the record to the nearest of the two repo roots; the journal is <root>/.artifact-journal.jsonl. (3) What does the hook actually compare? For every staged file matching jurisdiction.json: sha256 of the STAGED blob == the last journal entry's sha_after for that path, else refuse with the path, both shas, and the one-line fix (`cairn artifact hand-edit <path> --why`). (4) How is the caller class decided? Read /proc/self/cgroup via cairn.tools.cgroup; a segment matching cairn-*.service → gate; a segment matching the superclaude scope name (read from launchers/superclaude, never hard-coded) → cc; a session-*.scope with a controlling tty and no cairn unit above → akien; anything else → unknown, and unknown is a journaled entry AND a raised trouble, never a silent write. (5) Which existing doors become callers, at which line? Listed in the ticket by path: validation store (cairn/devices/tester store), history append (cairn/tools/base history door), ticket cast (skills/sorted resolve), trouble clear (TroubleDevice.clear), ruling open (cairn/machines/ruling). Each replaces its write_text with artifact.write and passes its own verb. (6) What about the 145 other write sites? They are the rename ticket's job; this ticket lands the door and the five callers, and the hook reds the rest at their next commit — that red is the rename ticket's worklist, by design. (7) Is the Claude Code deny rule part of this ticket? Yes: .claude/settings.json gains permissions.deny for Edit/Write on the jurisdiction globs, and the existing deletegate PreToolUse hook on Bash learns the same globs for redirections and sed -i. Both are defense in depth over the pre-commit check, which is the one that counts.
falsifier: DONE when, measured by cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/: (1) write_text to a jurisdiction path from each of the three caller classes without the door is refused at commit by the pre-commit hook (the working-copy sha is not the journal's last sha_after) — three teeth, one per caller class, each a real subprocess under a fixture cgroup or the real one; (2) the door, called from a systemd --user transient unit, from this superclaude scope, and from a pty login shell, journals caller=gate|cc|akien respectively — measured, not read from a field; (3) a chain break (an entry edited or removed) is detected by replaying the chain from the first entry; (4) `cairn artifact hand-edit <path> --why` parks the diff, opens a ruling packet through `cairn ruling open`, and leaves the record byte-identical until the ruling is confirmed; the door reverts it on `cairn ruling` refusal; (5) a proof's scratch record under a set_diagnostic_roots world never reaches the journal. WRONG INTENT if the door reads caller=unknown for any of the three in (2) — then identity must come from elsewhere and the journal is a log, not a gate. HORIZON: the three-caller measurement is the first proof written, before any hook; if it fails the ticket routes back to Akien with the measurement, not a workaround.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — 'records go through their door' is prose and a memory today; 145 code sites in 69 files write these paths with write_text); Law 7 (a record of truth never collapses an error — a hand edit IS a collapsed error, and 481221f45884 stands at [PROVED] with no crossing behind it); Law 6 (one owner gates writes; the door is the gate and the journal is who came through it); Law 10 (the caller is measured, not asked)

watchme.trigger: every append to either .artifact-journal.jsonl — the door pokes the probe after the write, so the probe costs nothing between writes and no poller exists (memory shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll).
watchme.enough: 500 journaled writes spanning all three caller classes with ZERO caller=unknown entries, AND the hand-edit escape route exercised at least once end to end (a ruling opened by the door and confirmed or refused by Akien). ONE unknown is the finding, not noise: it means a writer exists whose ancestry the door cannot read, which is the WRONG-INTENT clause of the falsifier. The watch does not clear on a timer.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, naming the caller-class histogram, every unknown entry with its raw cgroup path, and the hand-edit rulings opened.
watchme.nexus: the who-writes-what tree — the same journal the counting learning block (third ticket of the ruling) reads; this probe is that block's first consumer and defines the frequency table it will predict from.
watchme.consumer: Akien, and the counting learning block once cast.

owed_physics: The hook and the deny rules are policy a process can bypass (git commit --no-verify; a CC session with hooks off). The physics: the record roots owned by a second unix user, with the door the only path through the sudo relay. Tracked here as the IOU this ticket does not pay. Second hole: a CC launched outside superclaude reads as Akien; the launcher is the fix (superclaude is the one door to a CC session).

cast_checks.assumption_check: FOUR, named with their standing. (1) That cgroup ancestry distinguishes the three callers. MEASURED for two of three on 2026-09-13: a rack-launched gate sits under a cairn-*.service unit (cairn/tools/cgroup already reads /proc/self/cgroup and the launchers proof test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller depends on it), and this CC session sits under the superclaude scope (the OOM cap in superclaude is a cgroup cap, memory claude-oom-kills-the-box). UNMEASURED: Akien's login shell on a pty reads as session-N.scope with no cairn unit above it; the door's proof measures all three, and the first tooth to write is that one. (2) That a CC launched OUTSIDE superclaude reads as Akien. TRUE by construction and it is a HOLE, not an assumption to resolve here: the launcher is the fix (superclaude is the one door to a CC session, memory rescue-service), carried in the ticket as owed physics. (3) That one journal file appended per write does not turn the record repos into a commit-per-write storm. The journal is ONE file per repo root (CairnCommons/.artifact-journal.jsonl and cairn/.artifact-journal.jsonl), appended, committed with the records it describes by the same commit the pre-commit hook inspects. (4) That 'record of truth' is an enumerable set. It is, today: tickets/, troubles/, decisions/, questions/, slates/, ideas/ under CairnCommons and every state.json, history.json, intention+why.json and validations/*.json under cairn/ (census 2026-09-13: 839 files). The set is DECLARED in cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json, and the rename ticket collapses it to one extension so the declaration becomes a glob.

challenge_at_birth.back_up: proceed — ruled P0 by Akien 2026-09-13; sequencing is door first (works on .json day one), rename second through the door, counting block third
challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Looked. Deny-rules alone (permissions.deny on Edit/Write) are one line and zero build — but blind to Bash, which is the path this session was told to prefer; a hook on Bash alone is blind to git checkout/stash/merge. The pre-commit check is the smallest single point that sees all three, so the door + journal + hook is the minimal shape that is physics rather than policy. The physics upgrade beyond it — the record roots owned by a second unix user, doors through the sudo relay — is filed as the IOU, not built now.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That cgroup ancestry is readable from inside every caller and distinguishes the three: a CC session must actually sit under a superclaude scope (measured for the ground loop; not yet measured for a CC launched outside superclaude, e.g. from a bare terminal — that reads as Akien, which is the hole to close with the launcher), and an in-process machine caller under systemd must resolve to its unit. Also that the journal can live in git beside the records without every door write producing a commit-per-write storm — it appends to one file.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: In-house: 55dc1f3d799b (validation store door is the only path, PROVED — one class), e2efd2771343 (state/history append door + history_integrity sieve comparing working copy against HEAD — two classes, wrong baseline: a door write and a hand write look identical until commit), 23089d52d805 (casting rides a door, TICKETME:waiting), 47b9767d6faa (relational state through db_domain). This intent generalizes them into one door with caller identity; the per-class doors keep their verbs and become callers. Field: git's own object model (content-addressed, hash-chained) is the pattern the journal cites; Friston's free-energy loop is the pattern the third ticket cites — the door is a prediction ('a record changes only through a door') with a residual that escalates.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: Law 6 vs 'a tool has users, not owners': the door is a TOOL (no state of its own — the journal is the holder's, berthed beside the records it guards), so it gates nothing at its own address; the OWNER of each record class still gates through its verb. No collision with the harbor master's crossings journal: that records boats moving, this records bytes changing, and 481221f45884 is exactly the case where the two disagree and should. Not exclusive-and-terminal anywhere — a distinction to record: the harbor journal says what MOVED, the artifact journal says what was WRITTEN and by whom.

measured_at_build.built: cairn/tools/artifact (artifact.py, __main__.py, jurisdiction.json, hooks/pre-commit, probes/callers_are_known.py, intention+why.json, proofs/test_artifact_door.py + validations); bin/cmd/artifact, bin/cmd/artifactgate (+ bin/proofs/test_artifact_gate.py), wired in .claude/settings.json on Write/Edit/MultiEdit/Bash; the tester's pre-commit hook asks `cairn artifact check` first, blocking; genesis: CairnCommons 893 records, cairn 433 records, both chains verify from 'genesis'; the CairnCommons hook installed and its first commit (6e40224) passed under it.
deviations_from_the_cast_falsifier: (1) cast as three teeth, one per caller class; built as ONE class-independent tooth (test_a_record_edited_around_the_door_is_refused_at_the_commit_question) — the commit question reads bytes against the journal and never asks who edited, so a per-class tooth would measure nothing the one tooth does not. Clause (2) is where the class is measured.

(2) cast as 'a pty login shell' for akien; built as the LIVE processes in session-N.scope / app-*.scope (four measured at seal: pids 1808, 1809, 2525119, 2525662 → akien), because a pty shell spawned by this session is a child of the superclaude scope and correctly reads cc by ancestry — a forged akien would have been the hollow tooth. gate is measured under a real transient cairn-proof-artifact-<pid>.service; cc is this session's scope and a plain child of it.

(4) cast as 'opens a ruling packet through cairn ruling open'; built as PARK: hand-edit restores the journaled bytes and parks the proposed bytes under the door (`cairn artifact parked`); approve(id, words) is accepted only from a process measured akien (refused from cc by measurement in the proof), refuse discards. Why: `cairn ruling open` needs his verbatim words, which a park does not yet have — the park is what waits for them; the ruling packet is opened by him or on his words at approve time, not authored by the door.
the caller CLASS is kernel truth (cgroup ancestry); the call stack Akien asked for rides the entry as testimony (top six frames) and never decides trust.

measured.ancestry: systemd-run --user --scope moves a child into a new scope but does not reparent it — a scope CC forges to look like a desktop app still has the claude process (superclaude-<pid>.scope) as an ancestor and reads cc. Measured 2026-09-13 in the proof (tooth 'a scope CC forges to look like a desktop app STILL reads as cc — by ancestry').
measured.escape_not_closed: a scope plus a double fork (parent exits, child reparented to pid 1) would break the ancestry walk — that child reads by its own scope, and if the scope is named like an app it reads akien. Not built against; recorded here as the door's known escape, beside the two the cast already named (git commit --no-verify; CC launched outside superclaude).
measured.writers: 7 doors threaded (validation_store, charter/projector, trouble, ruling, transitions._write_ticket, saveslate door, idea door); the census's 145 write sites in 69 files still spell record paths with write_text — every one that is a real writer now lands REFUSED at commit, which is the instrument that finds them; the rename follow-on carries the sweep.
measured.gate_matches_command_text: bin/cmd/artifactgate reads the Bash command TEXT for a redirect/mv/cp/rm/sed -i/python open-for-write aimed at a record; a heredoc that merely mentions such a pattern is refused too (n=1 this session, a proof edit) — the trade is a split command, never a lost write.
